title: The Real Reason The 'Blood Moon' Turns Red
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real science behind why a total lunar eclipse turns the Moon red — it's the same atmospheric physics as a sunset, not an omen. The next one lights up the sky August 27-28.

hook_candidates.text: The 'Blood Moon' isn't red because of Mars, magic, or a bad omen — it's Earth's atmosphere acting like a giant lens.
Ever wonder why a total lunar eclipse turns the Moon blood red instead of just going dark?
Everyone calls it a rare 'Blood Moon' event — it's neither rare, nor really about the moon at all.

beats.text: The 'Blood Moon' isn't red because of Mars, magic, or a bad omen — it's Earth's atmosphere acting like a giant lens.
beats.broll_query: blood moon lunar eclipse night sky

beats.text: During a total lunar eclipse, Earth blocks the Sun's direct light, but sunlight still bends around the edges of our planet.
beats.broll_query: earth shadow lunar eclipse diagram animation

beats.text: That bent light passes through the atmosphere, which filters out blue and lets red and orange through — the same physics as every sunset.
beats.broll_query: sunset red sky atmosphere scattering light

beats.text: So the Moon isn't glowing red on its own — it's being lit by every sunrise and sunset on Earth happening at once.
